claim: History, not a forecast. Using Treasury yields as a stand-in for CD rates, we compared locking a 5-year rate with rolling a 1-year rate 5 times for every start month from 1953 to 2022 (833 starts). In the 132 start months when the 1-year yield was above the 5-year yield, locking the lower 5-year rate still ended with more money in 64.4% of them (median: 2.5% more money after 5 years; range -13.93% to +22.05%), about the same as across all start months (65.2%). Those inverted months fall into 23 separate episodes; locking came out ahead in most of the months of 14 of them. Rolling won when rates kept climbing after the inversion (mid-1960s, 1978-80, 2022); locking won big when rates fell (1980-82, 1989, 2000, 2006-07). On this record, a higher 1-year rate at the start did not mean rolling would end ahead. In Aug 2026 the 1-year Treasury yield was 4.03% and the 5-year 4.38%, so the Treasury curve itself was not inverted then; bank CD rate tables can differ from Treasury yields.

numbers.definition: Number of start months. Start month s runs over every month with a GS5 value from 1953-04-01 on, kept only if GS1 has values at s, s+12, s+24, s+36 and s+48 months (last start 2022-08-01). Lock = (1 + GS5(s)/100)^5. Roll = product over k=0..4 of (1 + GS1(s+12k)/100). 'Lock ahead' means Lock > Roll. 'Inverted start' means GS1(s) > GS5(s) (strictly). GS1 / GS5 = market yield on US Treasury securities at 1-year / 5-year constant maturity, quoted on an investment basis, percent, monthly averages, pinned FRED CSVs (coed=2026-08-01).

assumptions: Treasury constant-maturity yields (monthly averages) stand in for 1-year and 5-year CD rates; actual CD rates sit at different levels and the CD curve can be inverted when the Treasury curve is not.
Interest compounds once a year at the yield on the start date of each holding period; all money stays invested for exactly 5 years; no early withdrawal.
Taxes, fees and bank-specific rates are ignored.
Overlapping monthly start dates; inversion episodes defined as runs of consecutive inverted months.
